title: China-to-Kiribati EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Interoperability — IEC 62196 Type 2 / CCS2 Direction
rows.target_requirement: Kiribati follows a UK/IEC electrical legacy and the practical EV charging direction is IEC 62196 Type 2 for AC charging and CCS2 for DC fast charging. This is not an Americas J1772 / CCS1 market. Connector conformity should be confirmed in the MISE, PUB, tender, site-owner, or charge-point-operator specification for each project, but China GB/T connector hardware is physically incompatible with the IEC Type 2 / CCS2 ecosystem.
target_standards: IEC 62196-2 — AC Type 2 coupler dimensional compatibility
IEC 62196-3 — DC and AC/DC vehicle couplers, including CCS2 configuration
IEC 61851-1 — EV conductive charging system general requirements
IEC 61851-23 and IEC 61851-24 — DC EVSE and DC communication
rows.china_equivalent: China AC chargers use GB/T 20234.2 couplers and China DC chargers use GB/T 20234.3 couplers with GB/T 27930 CAN communication. GB/T AC connector geometry, gender, signaling, and contact arrangement differ from IEC 62196 Type 2, and GB/T DC couplers are not CCS2. GB/T charger hardware therefore cannot be treated as a connector-compatible substitute for Kiribati IEC deployments.
rows.gap: Conversion from GB/T to Kiribati IEC Type 2 / CCS2 requires hardware redesign of the coupler, cable, locking system, proximity-pilot and control-pilot circuits, labels, temperature-rise evidence, spare parts, and for DC chargers the communication stack from GB/T 27930 to the CCS2 / IEC 61851-24 / ISO 15118 direction where required. Adapters should not be treated as a project-compliant substitute.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where IEC 62196 Type 2 / CCS2 is specified by MISE, PUB, tender, site-owner, or CPO requirements; GB/T substitution is not physically compatible
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 20234 conformity applies to China domestic connector design and is not an IEC 62196 Type 2 / CCS2 substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Kiribati IEC Type 2 / CCS2 deployments require connector hardware and protocol redesign for GB/T chargers. This is an IEC / UK-legacy direction, not an Americas J1772 / CCS1 direction, and GB/T connectors cannot be accepted as plug-compatible.

source.publisher: Asian Development Bank (Kiribati energy project specifications)

rows.requirement: PUB Grid Connection — 240/415 V 50 Hz Island Network
rows.target_requirement: Kiribati electricity supply is operated by the Public Utilities Board (PUB Kiribati), with sector oversight by the Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy (MISE). The low-voltage context is 240 V single-phase / 415 V three-phase at 50 Hz. That is the same frequency as China but a different nominal voltage from China's 220/380 V baseline. Grid-connected charger projects should be treated as site-specific electrical installations requiring PUB supply-capacity review, protection coordination, metering, earthing, harmonic and power-quality review, commissioning, and written project acceptance before energisation.
target_standards: Public Utilities Board (PUB Kiribati) electricity network connection and project acceptance
MISE electricity-sector policy oversight
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
IEC 61851-1 — EV conductive charging system general requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic charger installations are commonly documented under GB/T 18487.1-2023, GB/T 20234 connector standards, GB/T 27930-2023 for DC communication, and local grid-operator acceptance. China domestic supply is 220 V single-phase / 380 V three-phase at 50 Hz. The shared 50 Hz frequency does not mean voltage equivalence: Kiribati 240/415 V requires input-voltage, protection-threshold, thermal, and metering validation beyond the China baseline.
china_standards: China local grid operator project-acceptance requirements
rows.gap: Exporters must confirm that the charger covers 240 V single-phase / 415 V three-phase at 50 Hz, not only China's 220/380 V settings. Protection thresholds, leakage-current devices, metering accuracy, harmonic emissions, supply-capacity calculations, earthing, surge protection, and commissioning documents should be prepared for PUB review. For small island grids and resort or solar-linked sites, load management and demand limits should be agreed with PUB before shipment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — grid-connected installations require PUB project review and acceptance; voltage is 240/415 V at 50 Hz, which differs from China 220/380 V despite the same frequency
mandatory_status.cn: China grid-operator acceptance applies domestically and is not a PUB approval substitute; China 220/380 V evidence must be revalidated for Kiribati 240/415 V

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Kiribati-ready EVSE needs PUB project acceptance and explicit 240/415 V 50 Hz validation. Do not describe the voltage as matching China: only the 50 Hz frequency matches, while nominal voltage differs from China's 220/380 V baseline.

rows.requirement: Kiribati Market Access — MISE / MISE / PUB Roles and Nascent EV Demand
rows.target_requirement: Kiribati is a small Pacific island economy with high-income tourism demand, strong solar and SIDS decarbonisation policy signals, and a nascent EV charging market. Relevant gates are split across MISE for standards, MISE for energy-sector regulation, and PUB for utility connection and installation acceptance. Importers should verify whether the charger model, HS code, smart/radio functions, labelling, and installation site trigger specific MISE conformity, MISE regulatory, customs, or PUB project-approval requirements before shipment.
target_standards: MISE energy-policy and donor-funded project-specification role
MISE energy-sector policy oversight
Public Utilities Board utility connection and installation acceptance
Kiribati renewable-energy and energy-efficiency policy context for SIDS decarbonisation
rows.china_equivalent: China EV charger suppliers commonly rely on domestic GB/T design evidence, China-market labelling, Chinese cloud or payment systems, and domestic operator references. These may support technical review but do not establish Kiribati market access. China CCC or GB/T documentation, if available, must be mapped to Kiribati project requirements, IEC evidence, importer responsibilities, and PUB connection approval.
rows.gap: Exporters should build a Kiribati package around the specific importer and site: IEC 61851 and IEC 62196 evidence, IEC 61000 EMC data, 240/415 V 50 Hz validation, coastal derating, English labelling and manuals, radio-module data, tariff or metering assumptions, spare-part support for islands, and written PUB / project-owner acceptance. Because the EV market is nascent, tender specifications may be more decisive than a mature national EVSE rulebook.

mandatory_status.target: Conditional — MISE, customs, radio, and PUB obligations depend on the product configuration, HS code, communications modules, and installation site; PUB acceptance is mandatory for grid-connected installations
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T or CCC status is not a Kiribati market-access substitute; documents must be remapped to Kiribati project, IEC, and utility requirements

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Kiribati is an opportunity market for IEC-aligned EV chargers, but exporters should not treat it as a paperwork-only extension of China GB/T supply. Confirm MISE, customs, radio-module, and PUB project requirements for the exact charger and site before shipment.

source.publisher: Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy (MISE)

rows.requirement: OCPP, EMC, Radio Modules, and Power Quality
rows.target_requirement: Networked EV chargers in Kiribati should be specified for OCPP back-office interoperability where a charge-point operator, resort operator, public-sector project, or PUB-linked programme requires remote monitoring, billing, diagnostics, or load management. Electrical and electronic emissions and immunity evidence should align with IEC 61000 EMC and power-quality standards. Cellular, Wi-Fi, RFID, payment, or smart-metering modules may trigger additional communications, spectrum, cybersecurity, and data-interface checks under project or national requirements.
target_standards: OCPP — Open Charge Point Protocol for networked EV chargers
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
IEC 61851-24 — digital communication between DC EV charging station and EV
Kiribati Communications Regulatory Authority or applicable spectrum authority requirements for radio modules where in scope
rows.china_equivalent: China DC fast chargers commonly use GB/T 27930-2023 CAN communication between the off-board charger and vehicle BMS. This is not OCPP back-office communication and is not the CCS2 communication direction. China-market chargers may also include China-specific payment, SIM, cloud, and operator integrations that need reconfiguration for Kiribati operators, roaming, language, currency, and data interfaces.
china_standards: China radio module approvals where applicable
rows.gap: Exporters must confirm the OCPP version, charge-point-management-system integration, remote diagnostics, load management, payment or RFID flow, SIM or communications module approval path, and IEC 61000 EMC reports for the final Kiribati configuration. For DC CCS2 products, GB/T 27930 must not be presented as the relevant communication evidence. Harmonic current and immunity data should be reviewed against the specific PUB supply point and island-grid constraints.

mandatory_status.target: Project-specific but commonly mandatory for networked public, resort, fleet, or utility-linked chargers; EMC and power-quality evidence is expected where required by MISE, PUB, tender, or site-owner specifications
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is China domestic DC vehicle-charger communication and is not OCPP or CCS2 back-office evidence

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Kiribati networked chargers should be validated for OCPP integration, IEC 61000 EMC and power quality, and local communications-module requirements. GB/T 27930 alone does not satisfy OCPP, CCS2 communication, or back-office interoperability needs.

source.publisher: Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy (MISE)

rows.requirement: IEC 61851 Safety and Coastal Environmental Derating
rows.target_requirement: Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Energy (MISE) is the energy ministry and policy lead, while MISE and PUB are key gates for energy-sector and grid-connected installations. EVSE safety evidence should be aligned with IEC 61851-1 for general conductive charging requirements and IEC 61851-23 for DC EVSE. Because Kiribati is a Pacific island state with humid, salt-laden coastal conditions, outdoor charger packages should include enclosure ingress protection, corrosion resistance, salt-mist review, surge protection, thermal derating, and maintenance instructions suitable for coastal and resort installations.
target_standards: IEC 61851-1 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 1: General requirements
IEC 61851-23 — DC electric vehicle supply equipment
IEC 60529 — Degrees of protection provided by enclosures (IP Code)
IEC 60068 environmental testing, including salt-mist and damp-heat context where specified
MISE energy-policy and donor-funded project-specification role
rows.china_equivalent: China's comparable design baseline is GB/T 18487.1-2023, supported by GB/T connector and DC communication standards. GB/T 18487 evidence is useful for engineering review but includes China-specific connector and communication assumptions and does not by itself establish IEC 61851 conformity for an IEC Type 2 / CCS2 Kiribati configuration. China domestic outdoor ratings may also need reassessment for Kiribati coastal salt, humidity, and surge exposure.
rows.gap: Exporters should prepare an IEC 61851 clause matrix, accredited IEC safety test reports for the final Type 2 / CCS2 configuration, IP and IK evidence, corrosion and salt-mist material review, surge-protection data, enclosure gasket and cable-gland specifications, thermal derating for humid coastal sites, and installation manuals aligned with PUB site conditions. A GB/T report for a China connector configuration is not enough.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory or project-specific — IEC safety evidence and environmental suitability are expected where specified by MISE-adopted standards, PUB connection requirements, MISE oversight, tender documents, or site-owner specifications
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 18487 applies to China domestic design and is not direct IEC 61851 evidence for Kiribati without a clause-level assessment and final-configuration testing

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat IEC 61851 and coastal environmental suitability as separate evidence items. Kiribati installations need final-configuration IEC safety evidence and salt-mist / humidity / surge review; China GB/T 18487 evidence alone is not enough.
